name: Protests against replacing MGNREGA with the VB-G RAM G Act
places: Nationwide; Congress protests at the AICC office, New Delhi
about: Parliament passed the VB-G RAM G Act in December 2025 to replace MGNREGA, the rural employment guarantee law. The Congress launched a 45-day MGNREGA Bachao Sangram on 10 January 2026, with fasts, village meetings, sit-ins and planned gheraos of state legislatures, and trade unions added the demand to their 12 February strike. In May the government announced that MGNREGA would be repealed on 1 July 2026.
demands: Repeal of the VB-G RAM G Act and restoration of MGNREGA as a rights-based law; protection of panchayats' role in rural work.

context.question: What replaced MGNREGA, and why do critics object?
context.short: In December 2025 Parliament replaced MGNREGA, the rural jobs guarantee law, with the VB-G RAM G Act. The Congress and trade unions campaigned for its repeal; the old law was set to end on 1 July 2026.
explainer: MGNREGA, the UPA-era rural employment law, gave rural households a legal right to wage work. Parliament passed the VB-G RAM G Act to replace it in December 2025, and the President assented on 21 December. The new Act guarantees 125 days of wage work per rural household a year, according to Deccan Herald.

The Congress launched a 45-day MGNREGA Bachao Sangram on 10 January 2026, with fasts, village meetings, sit-ins and planned gheraos of state assemblies, arguing that the change erodes a legal right. Trade unions added the restoration of MGNREGA to their 12 February strike.
In May the government announced that MGNREGA would be repealed on 1 July, with its assets, liabilities and records moving to the new scheme.
impact: MGNREGA's assets, liabilities and records move to the VB-G RAM G scheme from 1 July 2026, according to The Wire.
The new Act guarantees 125 days of work a year. Critics, including the Congress, say it still erodes the legal right to work and the role of panchayats.
